points.title: 乡村童年
points.description: 托马斯·哈代出生于多塞特郡的小镇博克汉普顿，在一个普通的石匠家庭长大。这段乡村生活经历深刻影响了他后来的文学创作，成为他描绘威塞克斯乡村世界的基础。哈代从小就展现出对文学和学习的热爱，尽管家庭条件有限，他仍接受了良好的基础教育，并开始阅读大量文学作品。这段时期他接触了莎士比亚、华兹华斯等经典作家，为他后来的文学创作奠定了基础。乡村生活的观察与体验，以及对社会底层人民的了解，成为他日后作品中反复出现的主题。
points.descriptionEn: Thomas Hardy was born in the small town of Bockhampton, Dorset, into a modest stonemason's family. This rural upbringing profoundly influenced his later literary works, forming the foundation for his depiction of the Wessex countryside. From an early age, Hardy showed a passion for literature and learning. Despite limited family means, he received a solid education and began reading extensively, including works by Shakespeare, Wordsworth, and other classic authors. These early experiences of rural life, his observations of the working class, and his understanding of rural poverty became recurring themes in his later works.

points.title: 都市求学
points.description: 1862年，哈代前往伦敦，在建筑师亚瑟·布洛姆菲尔德的事务所工作。这段时期他不仅学习了建筑专业知识，还广泛接触了城市文化和思想。哈代在伦敦度过了五年，期间他继续自学文学，并开始尝试写作。他阅读了大量当代文学作品，特别是法国现实主义和自然主义作品，这些对他后来的创作风格产生了深远影响。尽管在伦敦的生活充满挑战，但这段经历开阔了他的视野，使他能够将乡村与城市两种生活方式进行对比，为他日后作品中的人物塑造提供了丰富素材。
points.descriptionEn: In 1862, Hardy moved to London to work in the architectural firm of Arthur Blomfield. During this period, he not only acquired professional architectural knowledge but also immersed himself in urban culture and ideas. Hardy spent five years in London, continuing his self-education in literature and beginning to write himself. He read extensively contemporary works, particularly French realism and naturalism, which profoundly influenced his later writing style. Despite the challenges of London life, this experience broadened his horizons and allowed him to contrast rural and urban ways of life, providing rich material for his characterizations in later works.

points.title: 回归与创作
points.description: 1867年，哈代因健康原因返回多塞特郡，继续从事建筑工作。这一时期他开始更加专注于文学创作，发表了第一部小说《穷人与贵妇》(1874)，这部作品获得了成功，使他能够放弃建筑职业，全职从事写作。哈代将他对乡村生活的深刻理解与在伦敦获得的思想视野相结合，创作出独特的文学风格。他开始构思威塞克斯系列小说，以多塞特郡为背景，描绘乡村社会的生活与变迁。这一阶段标志着哈代从建筑师向小说家的转变，也是他文学创作风格形成的关键时期。
points.descriptionEn: In 1867, Hardy returned to Dorset due to health issues, continuing to work as an architect. During this period, he began to focus more on literary writing, publishing his first novel, 'Desperate Remedies' (1874). The success of this work allowed him to abandon architecture and pursue writing full-time. Hardy combined his deep understanding of rural life with the broader perspective gained in London, developing a unique literary style. He began conceiving his Wessex novels, set in Dorset, depicting rural society and its changes. This phase marked Hardy's transition from architect to novelist and was crucial in forming his distinctive literary voice.

points.title: 文学巅峰
points.description: 这一时期是哈代文学创作的黄金阶段，他创作了包括《卡斯特桥市长》(1886)、《德伯家的苔丝》(1891)、《无名的裘德》(1895)等经典作品。哈代在伦敦与多塞特之间往返，既享受都市的文化氛围，又保持与乡村的联系。他的作品深刻探讨了社会不公、道德观念、命运与偶然性等主题，引起了广泛讨论但也引发争议。特别是《无名的裘德》因其对宗教和婚姻制度的批判而受到强烈谴责，导致哈代转向诗歌创作。这一时期他建立了自己在英国文学界的重要地位，作品被翻译成多种语言，影响远及欧洲和美国。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked the peak of Hardy's literary career, during which he created masterpieces including 'The Mayor of Casterbridge' (1886), 'Tess of the d'Urbervilles' (1891), and 'Jude the Obscure' (1895). Hardy traveled between London and Dorset, enjoying both urban cultural life and maintaining his rural connections. His works deeply explored themes of social injustice, morality, fate, and chance, sparking widespread discussion but also controversy. 'Jude the Obscure' in particular faced strong condemnation for its criticism of religious and marital institutions, leading Hardy to shift focus to poetry. During this time, he established his significant position in British literature, with his works translated into multiple languages and influencing writers across Europe and America.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 1912年，哈代的妻子爱玛去世，这对他的创作产生了深远影响。他开始创作一系列悼亡诗，表达对亡妻的思念。这一时期哈代主要专注于诗歌创作，出版了《时光笑柄》(1914)等诗集。第一次世界大战期间，他创作了反战诗歌，表现出对人类命运的深刻思考。1923年，哈代完成了他的最后一部小说《心爱的人》，之后基本停止小说创作。1928年，哈代在多塞特郡逝世，享年87岁。他的葬礼在威斯敏斯特教堂举行，但按照他的遗愿，心脏被带回多塞特郡安葬。哈代去世后，他的作品被重新评价，被视为英国文学传统的重要组成部分，对现代主义文学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1912, Hardy's wife Emma died, profoundly affecting his writing. He began composing a series of elegiac poems expressing his grief for his lost wife. During this period, Hardy focused primarily on poetry, publishing collections such as 'Moments of Vision' (1914). During World War I, he wrote anti-war poetry, demonstrating his deep reflections on human destiny. In 1923, Hardy completed his final novel, 'The Well-Beloved,' after which he largely ceased novel writing. Hardy died in Dorset in 1928 at the age of 87. His funeral was held at Westminster Abbey, but according to his wishes, his heart was returned to Dorset for burial. After his death, Hardy's works were re-evaluated and recognized as an essential part of the British literary tradition, exerting profound influence on modernist literature.

supporter.zh: 哈代被誉为英国文学史上最伟大的小说家和诗人之一，他的作品深刻揭示了维多利亚时代的社会矛盾和道德困境。支持者认为哈代通过威塞克斯系列小说，真实记录了乡村社会的变迁，为底层人民发声。他的诗歌作品同样具有高度艺术价值，特别是晚期的悼亡诗，情感真挚，语言优美。哈代对命运、偶然性和社会不公的探讨，展现了他对人类处境的深刻理解，使他超越了时代局限，成为永恒的文学经典。
supporter.en: Hardy is celebrated as one of the greatest novelists and poets in English literary history, whose works profoundly reveal the social contradictions and moral dilemmas of the Victorian era. Supporters argue that through his Wessex novels, Hardy authentically documented the transformation of rural society and gave voice to the working class. His poetic works, particularly his later elegies, possess significant artistic value with their sincere emotion and beautiful language. Hardy's exploration of fate, chance, and social injustice demonstrates his deep understanding of the human condition, allowing him to transcend temporal limitations and achieve literary immortality.

critic.zh: 批评者指出哈代的作品存在悲观主义倾向，过度强调命运的无情和人类努力的徒劳。他们认为哈代对宗教和婚姻制度的批判过于激进，缺乏建设性意见。此外，哈代作品中女性角色的塑造也受到质疑，有评论认为他将女性主要描绘为受害者或牺牲品，缺乏复杂性。一些批评者还认为哈代的叙事风格过于沉重，缺乏必要的希望和救赎元素，使读者感到压抑和绝望。
critic.en: Critics point out that Hardy's works exhibit excessive pessimism, emphasizing the cruelty of fate and the futility of human effort. They argue that his criticism of religious and marital institutions was too radical and lacked constructive alternatives. Additionally, the portrayal of female characters in Hardy's works has been questioned, with some critics suggesting he primarily depicted women as victims or sacrifices without sufficient complexity. Some also contend that Hardy's narrative style is overly somber, lacking necessary elements of hope and redemption, leaving readers feeling depressed and hopeless.

objective.zh: 从历史和文化视角看，哈代被视为维多利亚时代向现代主义过渡的关键人物。他的作品既保留了维多利亚时期的现实主义传统，又预示了现代主义对内心世界的关注。在流行文化中，哈代的作品被多次改编为电影、电视剧和戏剧，特别是《德伯家的苔丝》和《卡斯特桥市长》已成为经典改编对象。哈代的威塞克斯世界不仅是一个文学创造，也成为英国文化的重要象征，代表了对乡村生活的怀旧与反思。他的作品持续影响着当代作家，被广泛研究，成为文学教育的重要组成部分。
objective.en: From a historical and cultural perspective, Hardy is viewed as a pivotal figure in the transition from Victorianism to modernism. His works both preserved the realist tradition of the Victorian era and anticipated modernism's focus on inner worlds. In popular culture, Hardy's works have been adapted numerous times into films, TV series, and plays, with 'Tess of the d'Urbervilles' and 'The Mayor of Casterbridge' becoming particularly notable adaptations. Hardy's Wessex world has become not just a literary creation but an important cultural symbol representing nostalgia for and reflection on rural life. His works continue to influence contemporary writers and are widely studied, forming an essential part of literary education.

self.zh: 人生不是由偶然和巧合构成的，而是由设计构成的。
self.en: Chance is not a thing but a mere word expressing the complex and unknown causation of effects of which we are ignorant.

others.zh: 哈代是英国文学中最伟大的悲剧作家，他的作品展现了人类在命运面前的挣扎与无奈。
others.en: Hardy is the greatest tragic writer in English literature, whose works show the struggle and helplessness of humanity in the face of fate.
